questions.question: Who talks to the agent and what do they want it to accomplish?
questions.why: Real users and tasks anchor the design.

questions.question: Which requests are outside its job even if it could answer?
questions.why: Scope limits stop it from promising the wrong help.

questions.question: When should it hand the conversation to a person?
questions.why: Some situations need a human decision.

exit_criteria: State the users, supported work and cases that need a human.

questions.question: Which assistant or app should be able to install this first?
questions.why: The target host sets the setup steps.

questions.question: Which sites or tools should it be allowed to contact?
questions.why: An allowlist makes the data boundary explicit.

questions.question: Who will control its installation and private settings?
questions.why: A clear owner can change or remove access later.

exit_criteria: Name the install target, its local scope and who controls access.

questions.question: Which information may the agent use to answer?
questions.why: Explicit sources help limit exposure and guessing.

questions.question: What actions can change something, and who approves each one?
questions.why: A user needs control over consequential actions.

questions.question: What should it remember across chats, and for how long?

exit_criteria: Record access to knowledge, permission for each tool, and retention choices.

questions.question: What should its tone sound like to someone asking for help?
questions.why: Examples are easier to test than adjectives.

questions.question: What should it say when it cannot verify an answer?
questions.why: A useful uncertain response can prevent guesswork.

questions.question: What happens after repeated failures or when someone asks for a person?
questions.why: The conversation needs a clear way to recover.

exit_criteria: Record a normal flow, uncertainty handling and handoff conversation.

questions.question: Which channel should we support first?
questions.why: The channel sets how people interact and what the system can show.

questions.question: How much cost and waiting time per conversation is acceptable?
questions.why: Clear limits help choose a model and fallback.

questions.question: What should a user see if the model or a tool is unavailable?
questions.why: The agent should explain where it stopped.

exit_criteria: Confirm channel, response-time and spend limits and a safe fallback.

questions.question: Which real conversations should become repeatable tests?
questions.why: Good answers can be compared to agreed examples.

questions.question: Which unsafe or out-of-scope requests must get a clear refusal?
Who can decide whether the responses are accurate and helpful?
questions.why: Release criteria need a person who can judge them.

exit_criteria: Provide examples for good answers, refusals, tool permission checks and human handoffs.

release_check.procedure: Install the agent in a clean supported harness. Run one approved representative task and capture its expected output and any required approval.
